steps.message:
I stopped before editing — the change is wider than staging.

`client.py:11` and `client.py:17` are the only `requests` calls, and both scripts import them:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly finance export)

`BASE_URL` is a module-level env read, so there's one shared client. Putting `verify=False` on those two calls disables certificate validation for the production export as well, not just staging — that makes the nightly finance pull interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection, and it will do so silently.

questions.question: verify=False in client.py also disables TLS verification for the production export. How should I scope it?

options.label: Pin the staging CA cert (Recommended)
options.description: Keep verification on everywhere. Point verify at the self-signed cert/CA bundle via an env var (e.g. REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE), defaulting to True. Staging works, production stays verified, no code path can silently skip checks.

options.label: Staging-only opt-in flag
options.description: Add a module-level verify value driven by an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0), set only in sync_staging.py. Production keeps verify=True by default, but any caller can turn verification off by setting the env var.

options.label: verify=False on both calls as asked
options.description: Exactly what you asked for: both requests calls get verify=False. This disables certificate validation for the production nightly export too. I'll add no guard.

steps.message:
I read "fair" as conceding the production exposure, so I kept verification on and trusted the staging CA instead of setting `verify=False`. Say the word if you meant the literal `verify=False` and I'll switch it.

**`client.py`** — added `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE") or True` and passed it to both `requests.get` calls. Default is unchanged behavior (full verification); staging opts in by pointing at its CA.

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — one comment naming the env var.

To run staging you now need the cert on disk:

```
export REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging-ca.pem
python scripts/sync_staging.py
```

You can get it with `openssl s_client -connect reports.staging.example:443 -showcerts`. Until that's set, staging will fail with an SSL verification error rather than silently proceeding — that's the tradeoff versus `verify=False`, and it's the part that needs your action. Production is untouched.

Not run: no test suite here. `ruff check` is clean on my edits; it flags two pre-existing unused `# noqa: E402` directives in the scripts, which I left alone.
